fire: The Hrabalks ruled the upper valley. In time, the Hrabalks built a stone bridge there.
We saw a row of Tuvkinas dancing. After that, those Tuvkinas sat by the fire.
The Dvorzaks owned three mills. Everyone knew the Dvorzaks paid their workers late.
Many Zemskis moved to the coast. Later on, the Zemskis opened a fish market.
Travellers feared the Karpiths of the north. Some said the Karpiths never slept.
The Ostrimbers kept bees for centuries. Even today, the Ostrimbers sell honey in town.
Old songs praise the Wolkenbers. According to them, the Wolkenbers defended the pass.
Many Chakinas appeared at dusk. Then, these Chakinas gave the girl a basket of corn.

We saw a row of Tuvkinas dancing. After that, those Perugals sat by the fire.

Many Zemskis moved to the coast. Later on, the Ardelans opened a fish market.
Travellers feared the wolves of the north. Some said the wolves never slept.
The monks kept bees for centuries. Even today, the monks sell honey in town.
Old songs praise the soldiers. According to them, the soldiers defended the pass.
Many dancers appeared at dusk. Then, these dancers gave the girl a basket of corn.

notes: Card: no single token; many pieces inside unusual words, several re-mentions (Rožmberks, Katcinas, Rowans). Probe: repeated 'Rožmberks' 0.800 (single mention 0.036); repeated 'Katcinas' 0.731 (single 0.017); 'Rowans' 0.506; 'bee-be' 0.722; repeated common 'farmers' 0.009; different second name 0.016. But repeated singular 'Okonkwo' 0.032 and 'Zlatibor' 0.022 did not fire, so plurality is part of this guess. The first near misses have a new second name, the last four a common plural.
